# JailBee

> JailBee runs isolated, per-branch development environments in Incus system
> containers. Every git branch gets a full container of its own — its own
> services, its own Docker daemon, its own IP, and optionally its own IDE and
> browser on your desktop — so several stacks run in parallel on one Linux
> host without port conflicts, Docker name clashes or shared-database
> collisions. It is also a sandbox for coding agents: the container is the
> boundary, so an agent can run unattended with permission prompts turned off.

JailBee is a Python CLI (`jailbee`, short form `jb`) that wraps the `incus`
command. It is project-agnostic: every repository supplies its own committed
`.jailbee/config.yaml` declaring what its containers need — bind mounts,
devices, egress allowlist, shared caches, and what boots on create. Install
with `uv tool install jailbee` or `pipx install jailbee`.

Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later. Built at GISGRO Oy, which is its origin, not its
scope.

## What makes it different

- **Isolation by boundary, not by allowlist.** Most agent sandboxes enumerate
  which paths, hosts and syscalls are permitted, so every new tool the agent
  reaches for is a policy change. JailBee moves the boundary instead: the
  container is the fence, and what happens inside it is unconstrained.
- **A system container, not an application container.** It runs its own init,
  its own Docker daemon (nested, `security.nesting`), its own systemd
  services. The repo's existing `docker-compose.yml` runs unmodified.
- **Per-container egress allowlist** enforced by a kernel-level ACL, written
  as hostnames and ports (`api.example.com:443`) rather than IP ranges, and
  covering any protocol — `ssh`, `git+ssh` and database clients included, not
  just HTTP. `github.com` is deliberately absent from the strict default so an
  unattended agent cannot surprise-push.
- **The container is a git remote.** `jailbee git push/pull/fetch/checkout/diff`
  move commits between host and container without a round trip through GitHub.
  Submodules travel with the superproject. `jailbee pr` opens or updates the
  GitHub PR from a container's branch, with the title and body written by the
  in-container Claude — to the project's own standard when the repo states one
  in `claude.pr_prompt`.
- **Host services reach in, opt-in.** A declared forward
  (`host_ports: [{ name: adb, port: 5037 }]`) makes a host service reachable on
  every container's own localhost — an adb server with a phone attached, a
  database — and `jailbee port` adds or removes one ad hoc, in either
  direction. Forwards are Incus proxy devices, so they bypass the egress ACL by
  construction; `jailbee net status` lists the open ones next to the allowlist.
- **One dashboard across every repo.** A live TUI (`jailbee dashboard`) or Qt
  GUI (`jailbee gui`) lists every container on the host and acts on it — shell,
  tmux, IDE, create or update the PR, update from base, read the diff, follow a
  background job's log — each offered only when it would do something.
- **GUI passthrough.** A JetBrains IDE and Chrome run *inside* the container
  and render on the host's Wayland session, reaching the container's own
  `localhost:3000`. Five containers can each serve port 3000 with nothing to
  forward and no collisions.
- **Snapshots** before an agent run, restore after.

## When not to use it

- **Not on macOS or Windows.** Linux only; the macOS path runs JailBee inside
  a Linux VM and is experimental.
- **Not if you need a hypervisor boundary.** A system container shares the
  host kernel, so a kernel bug is an escape path. Docker Sandboxes (`docker
  sbx`) gives a microVM with its own kernel and is the stronger boundary.
- **Not if your stack is one process and one database.** `git worktree` plus
  `docker compose -p` is free and already installed.
- **Not free to adopt.** Host setup (Incus, UID delegation, firewall, kernel
  keyring limits) is a one-time afternoon, and the golden image takes 10–15
  minutes to build once per repo stack.
- **No editor set up for you beyond JetBrains.** `jailbee ide` accepts the
  JetBrains launcher names and there is no Dev Containers integration. VS Code
  is not ruled out — the GUI passthrough is generic, so installing it into the
  golden image and launching it from a shell works — but nothing ships to wire
  it up.

## Documentation

- [Installation](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/installation.md): one-time host setup — Incus, UID delegation, installing the CLI
- [Getting started](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md): concepts, configuring a repo, building the image, a typical day
- [Commands](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/commands.md): full command and flag reference
- [Git bridge](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/git-bridge.md): host↔container git bridge, stacked PRs, PR review
- [Configuration reference](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/config.md): every `.jailbee/config.yaml` and `global.yaml` key
- [Generic agent support](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/agents.md): the `agents:` config key, the six shipped presets (Claude Code plus five untested templates), and how to add one of your own
- [Security and limitations](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/security.md): isolation model and known limits, including what running an agent without prompts does and does not cover
- [Who JailBee is for](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/comparison.html): how it compares to Dev Containers, BranchBox, nono and Docker Sandboxes, when not to use it, and what it costs
- [Full technical comparison](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/comparison.md): the same comparison at length, with every caveat and the sources each claim was checked against
- [Architecture](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): how the pieces fit together

## Optional

- [Setting up JailBee in your own project](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/project-config.md): adapting it to your own repo and stack
- [Running on macOS](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/macos.md): via a Linux VM, experimental
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md): common failures by symptom
